risks.note: The Indian logistics market is highly fragmented with many unorganised players; Navkar relies on differentiation through integrated, technology-enabled, multimodal solutions (Category 1 CTO licence, large-format CFS/ICD footprint, PFT infrastructure) that smaller players cannot easily replicate at scale.

The ICD and CFS business is inherently linked to Indian EXIM trade performance, which is influenced by global economic conditions; mitigated by growing domestic cargo (35-45 percent YoY growth at Morbi ICD in FY 2025-26) to reduce dependence on ocean freight cycles.

Ongoing Middle East conflict, US tariff policies and the Russia-Ukraine situation continue to introduce volatility in global shipping routes, freight rates and EXIM trade volumes, with a potential cascading effect on Indian port and CFS throughput.

Growing reliance on Indian Railways through the CTO and PFT businesses means disruptions to rail services, rake availability or policy changes could impact operations; mitigated via an owned rake fleet supplemented by leased rakes and relationships with railway authorities.

The growing share of DPD containers, which bypass CFSs and move directly from port to factory, represents a structural challenge to CFS volumes, though many DPD containers still require CFS facilities for interim storage and customs processing.
Increased capacity by competing CFS, ICD and rail operators, and development of new terminals, creates pricing pressure and potential market-share competition.

risks.risk: Mundra Port congestion / rail evacuation efficiency
risks.note: Increasing congestion at Mundra Port has at times affected rail evacuation efficiency from the Saurashtra hinterland; as Morbi ICD volumes grow, seamless rail connectivity to Mundra remains critical.

As a technology-enabled logistics provider operating EDI, OCR, GPS and digital tracking systems, Navkar is exposed to technology failure and cybersecurity risks, mitigated through IT infrastructure, access controls and system monitoring.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Filing basis] Navkar filed this under Regulation 30 as the "latest investor presentation released by the Ultimate Holding Company of Navkar Corporation Limited i.e. JSW Infrastructure Limited" — so nearly every figure is JSW Infrastructure group/parent, not Navkar standalone; only the slides explicitly naming Navkar Corporation are entity-specific.
- [Regulation] The deck details two Indian Railways licence regimes central to the logistics plan — GPWIS (launched 2018, general-purpose wagons, coal/cement/ore/petroleum) and LSFTO (launched 2020, specialised wagons for steel, chemicals, fly ash, edible oil, alumina) — described as a shift from a state-controlled model to a public-private partnership framework.
- [Anchor customer] JSW Steel is presented as the strong anchor customer, including a long-term take-or-pay agreement for the Odisha slurry pipeline and the 36 mtpa Dharamtar/Jaigarh expansion being predicated on a 5 mtpa steel-making capacity expansion of the anchor customer at Dolvi.
- [New award] Secured another PPP project at Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port with capacity of 0.9 million TEUs; also secured Environmental Clearance and rail connectivity approval to the DFC for Murbe Port, Maharashtra.
- [Sector backdrop] Indian port capacity is projected to rise from 2,810 mtpa in FY26 to 3,500 mtpa by FY30E and 10,000 mtpa by FY47E; infrastructure capital expenditure is shown rising to ₹ 12.2 trillion in FY27E.
